state.question: In which video is there an unnecessary action that should not have been performed during assembly?
state.summary: Requirements remain open. The strongest local candidate for an unnecessary assembly action is the v3 internal-component screwdriver adjustment, because its necessity is explicitly uncertain; v2 separation and v1 unscrewing do not better support their option labels.
inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.

attempts: Local v2 evidence shows body/chassis separation and adjustment, but necessity for access or installation is not established.
Local v3 evidence shows handling and screwdriver adjustment of an internal black component inside the body, with explicit uncertainty about necessity for final assembly.
Local v1 evidence shows unscrewing chassis parts, but whether this was unnecessary versus required attachment remains unclear.
